- **G? [M] Walk notes: the owner's own walks steer the loop** (2026-11-20) · no surface · the owner's calls
  Area: process (tend). From: /investigate, the owner's ask (2026-11-20). Brief: docs/research/walk-notes.md.
  Calls: kept in the repository with places stripped; a free line, then prompts for what is missing; steers the lens, the sweeps and silence; a report line, no reminder. Decision 0238.
  Done when: after the owner's next walk, `/walked` with one sentence stores a note naming an area and a kind, the committed line holds no street, town or time of day, and the next `/tend` run's report cites it (a sweep of that area first, or a drafted line marked "seen on a walk").
  Touches: decisions 0005 (local-only, in spirit: the owner's whereabouts in a public repository), 0236 (expectation lines), 0229 (`next`), 0157 (only the owner ratifies).
  The slice: 1. `/walked <anything>` is an owner-only skill (`disable-model-invocation`): it takes a sentence, dictation or a screenshot and sorts what it says into reached for, got in the way and keep, each with an area from `scripts/features.js` (or `app` when none fits). 2. It asks once, in one round, only about what the line did not say, "nothing" always an option; a note with only one kind is a whole note. 3. Before committing, it shows the owner the words it will store; a screenshot is never committed, only its observations in words. 4. `scripts/walks.js add` appends to `.claude/skills/tend/walks.jsonl` (day, area, kind, words) and refuses a line holding a street, a town from the gazetteer, coordinates or a time of day, with the words that tripped it; `list` reads the window. 5. A "reached for" note becomes a drafted expectation line for its area marked "seen on a walk <day>", put to the owner ahead of model-drafted lines and never ratified by the proxy. 6. A "got in the way" note puts its area first in `next` until a sweep of that area has run since the note. 7. A "keep" note protects what it names: a refinement that would change it is filed `[owner]`, not shipped. 8. `/tend`'s report and the orchestrator's insights say once when no note has come in for 14 days; nothing else reminds. 9. Tests for `walks.js` (the place refusals, append-only), `next`'s order and the lens's tagging; the skills map and `records audit 14`'s list say the same.
  Precedent: diary studies (an entry just after the event, anchored to it); a dogfooding friction log; Strava's optional "How did that activity feel?" and Apple Journal's prompts (all unverified; docs/research/adjacent-apps.md, "Ask how it went, just after"). Departs from Strava: words, never a number.
  Payoff: the loop's priorities and expectations rest on real use, the one thing a local-only app cannot otherwise know. Cost: M; about eight files (a new skill, a new script and its test, `scripts/tend.js`, three skill files, the map); no native code. Reopens: tend. After it: "settled after three walks", once G6 computes states.
  Instead: criteria 1, 3 and 4 alone (notes kept, read by hand in each run's report).
